attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing theorem is a gauge-invariant nonperturbative boundary OPE/renormalization result for reflected Wilson collar products at the reflection plane. Current RG compactness controls fixed collars but does not yet prove that the connected finite boundary kernel B vanishes or is separable after all same-theory Wilson renormalizations.
steps: Start with a finite Wilson core {W(C_i)} in the positive half-space closure and apply collaring T_\delta so every observable has support in t>\delta. For each cutoff, reflection positivity gives Q_{a,L,\delta}(c)\ge0.

Use the RG-to-OS passage only for fixed collars: S_{a,L}(\Theta W(T_\delta C_i)W(T_\delta D_j)) converges to N^\delta_{ij}, and the closed positive cone gives N^\delta\ge0. Taking \delta\downarrow0 entrywise gives N\ge0 when the trace limit is controlled.
Compare N with the intended plane-touching target matrix M. The most general boundary discrepancy compatible with earlier cycles is N=\Gamma\circ M+A, with A additive and \Gamma multiplicative.

Invoke diagonal trace continuity. If A is a positive boundary OS contribution, finite-dimensional Cauchy-Schwarz gives A=0. This removes additive contacts unless positivity of the boundary OPE itself fails.

Write \log\Gamma_{ij}=\alpha_i+\overline{\alpha_j}+B(\beta_i,\beta_j). The one-body terms are exactly diagonal congruences and cancel from K_{ik;jl}. Thus K is the finite difference of only the connected boundary footprint interaction B.

If the footprints are separated, locality predicts B=0; then \Gamma_{ij}=d_i\overline{d_j}, so N=DMD^* and M\ge0 follows. This part of the OS bridge is valid provided the local anomaly decomposition is valid.

For coincident footprints, test B perturbatively by the reflected Wilson product. At leading gauge-field order a possible connected term has the schematic form B(C,D)\sim g^2 C_2\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\left[\int_{\partial C\times\partial D}\frac{\dot\gamma(s)\cdot\dot\eta(t)}{|\gamma(s)-\eta(t)|^2+(2\delta)^2}\,ds\,dt-\text{one-body perimeter/cusp subtractions}\right]. If the remaining finite part has nonzero four-point finite difference, K\ne0 and the same-theory bridge fails.

The derivation therefore reduces the analytic Yang-Mills problem to a boundary OPE statement: prove the connected post-subtraction kernel B has zero finite differences on a dense Wilson core, or exhibit a nonzero K.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The argument is valid as finite-dimensional linear algebra once the anomaly decomposition and locality/support statement for B are assumed. It is not yet a Yang-Mills proof because those assumptions are precisely the hard analytic content: one must control Wilson-loop trace limits, cusp/hairpin singularities, and possible pair-dependent boundary counterterms without gauge fixing changing the test algebra.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: Wilson Boundary Cross-Ratio Localization

assumptions: For each fixed collar width \delta>0 and finite coefficient vector c, Q_{a,L,\delta}(c)=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j S_{a,L}(\Theta W(T_\delta C_i)W(T_\delta D_j))\ge0, and the cutoff-removal topology is valid for these reflected Wilson products.
The fixed-collar continuum limit exists: N^\delta_{ij}=S(\Theta W(T_\delta C_i)W(T_\delta D_j)) and N^\delta\to N entrywise along \delta\downarrow0 for the finite matrix under study.
Diagonal trace continuity is locked in the same theory: N_{ii}=\Gamma_{ii}M_{ii} with \Gamma_{ii}>0 and no independent additive diagonal contact term.
Any additive boundary contact matrix A appearing in N=\Gamma\circ M+A is positive semidefinite as a boundary OS contribution; hence zero diagonal forces A=0.

The multiplicative anomaly admits a local footprint decomposition \log\Gamma_{ij}=\alpha_i+\overline{\alpha_j}+B(\beta_i,\beta_j), where B(\beta_i,\beta_j)=0 when the two boundary footprints are separated by a positive distance in the reflection plane.
The one-body terms \alpha_i are valid same-theory renormalizations, i.e. they implement an invertible diagonal congruence rather than changing the target Schwinger functions.
definitions: source object: cutoff reflection-positive gauge-invariant Schwinger functionals S_{a,L} on a locked positive-time Wilson/core algebra, with collar maps T_\delta pushing plane-touching observables into t>\delta.

target object: continuum gauge-invariant Schwinger functional S on the same Wilson/core algebra, satisfying OS positivity for finite reflected quadratic forms including observables with support at the reflection plane.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, first for fixed collars through the closed cone topology and then through a boundary trace theorem for Wilson OS matrices.

same-theory condition: Wilson-loop renormalizations and observable embeddings are fixed before the collar limit; allowed boundary factors are only one-body diagonal congruences already built into that identification, never pair-dependent counterterms introduced to repair positivity.

equations.label: fixed-collar OS matrix
equations.latex: N^\delta_{ij}=S(\Theta W(T_\delta C_i)W(T_\delta D_j)),\qquad \sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j N^\delta_{ij}\ge0
equations.valid_when: The Wilson loops after collaring lie strictly in positive/negative time and the regulated reflection positivity survives the RG limit for these fixed reflected probes.

equations.label: boundary anomaly decomposition
equations.valid_when: The collar limit exists entrywise and the only loss between the collar matrix and the intended target matrix is a multiplicative Wilson boundary factor plus a separately positive additive contact contribution.

equations.label: additive contact vanishing
equations.valid_when: The boundary contact term is itself an OS-positive matrix and diagonal trace continuity has already removed diagonal contact defects.

equations.label: cross-ratio detector
equations.valid_when: The logarithmic anomaly decomposition is valid; one-body congruence terms cancel exactly.

equations.label: rank-one transfer
equations.valid_when: The finite anomaly matrix has nonzero entries and the vanishing cross-ratio holds on the finite Wilson OS matrix under consideration.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A concrete falsifier is a four-loop Wilson collar family with separated boundary footprints but nonzero K, or with coincident footprints whose post-subtraction connected boundary OPE gives K\ne0; either shows the bridge preserved positivity only after changing the theory.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns the abstract closed-cone OS passage into a finite Wilson boundary theorem: positivity is already valid for collars, and same-theory positivity at the plane is equivalent to absence of a connected nonseparable boundary anomaly.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Boundary-footprint localization bridge for Wilson OS anomalies. For a finite mirror-smooth Wilson core, let N_{ij}=lim_{\delta\downarrow0} S(\Theta W(T_\delta C_i) W(T_\delta D_j)) be the collar OS matrix and M_{ij}=S(\Theta W(C_i)W(D_j)) the intended target matrix. Assume diagonal trace continuity, no positive additive contact defect, and a local multiplicative anomaly representation \Gamma_{ij}=\exp(\alpha_i+\overline{\alpha_j}+B(\beta_i,\beta_j)), where \beta_i,\beta_j are reflection-plane boundary footprints and B is supported only on coincident footprints. Then every separated-footprint finite OS matrix transfers positivity by a rank-one congruence; equivalently the logarithmic cross-ratio K_{ik;jl} vanishes. Thus the only remaining same-theory obstruction is a connected coincident-footprint boundary OPE term detected by K\ne0.

assumptions: The boundary contact term is separately represented by a positive semidefinite quadratic form, rather than only by an indefinite remainder after subtractions.
The same-theory observable identification fixes individual Wilson loop normalizations, so diagonal contact terms cannot be hidden in a changed target observable.
The finite matrix is Hermitian, as required for an OS quadratic form.
definitions: A finite OS matrix is M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_iF_j) for a fixed finite list of positive-time gauge-invariant observables.
An additive boundary contact is a matrix A_{ij} supported at the reflection plane in the trace limit N=\Gamma\circ M+A.
Diagonal trace continuity means A_{ii}=0 after the same-theory renormalization of each individual observable.
OS-positive contact means \sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_jA_{ij}\ge0 for every finite coefficient vector c.

equations.label: contact Cauchy-Schwarz
equations.valid_when: A is a positive semidefinite finite Hermitian matrix.

equations.label: zero diagonal kills contact
equations.valid_when: Diagonal trace continuity is valid for all observables in the chosen finite Wilson core.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A claimed positive additive mixed contact with zero diagonal is a falsifier of one of the hypotheses: either diagonal trace continuity failed, the contact is not positive, or the observable algebra was changed.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Removes additive contacts from the main obstruction list, so the discovery pressure focuses on multiplicative nonrank-one Wilson anomalies.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Positive additive contact elimination lemma. If the difference between the collar OS matrix and the multiplicatively renormalized target OS matrix is an additive boundary contact matrix A which is OS-positive, then diagonal trace continuity eliminates all additive contact terms, not just the diagonal ones.

assumptions: The multiplicative relation N=\Gamma\circ M has no additive contact term, by Lemma cycle-0187-L2 or an equivalent estimate.
The finite Wilson core contains enough variation that the bridge should not rely on accidental positivity of one matrix N.
The anomaly entries are nonzero and Hermitian-compatible: \Gamma_{ji}=\overline{\Gamma_{ij}}.
definitions: The Schur inverse \Gamma^{[-1]} has entries 1/\Gamma_{ij} wherever \Gamma_{ij}\ne0.
Universal same-theory transfer means positivity must hold for every possible collar-limit OS matrix N generated by the locked test algebra, not only for a single accidental matrix.
A logarithmic cross-ratio K measures failure of rank-one factorization of the multiplicative anomaly.
A positive Schur multiplier is a matrix H such that H\circ P\ge0 for every positive semidefinite matrix P of the same finite size.

equations.label: Schur transfer condition
equations.latex: N\ge0,\quad M=\Gamma^{[-1]}\circ N\quad\text{is guaranteed positive for all }N\ge0\iff \Gamma^{[-1]}\text{ is a positive Schur multiplier}
equations.valid_when: The bridge is required uniformly on the finite OS cone, not merely for a special matrix.

equations.label: rank-one criterion
equations.latex: K_{ik;jl}=0\ \forall i,k,j,l\quad\iff\quad \Gamma_{ij}=d_i\overline{d_j}\text{ on the finite index set}
equations.valid_when: All anomaly entries are nonzero so logarithms and cross-ratios are defined consistently.

equations.label: two-by-two damping falsifier
equations.valid_when: This illustrates that a single positive output is not enough; the valid obstruction is universal Schur positivity, equivalently no nonrank-one anomaly under the two-sided positivity hypothesis.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A nonzero K together with a collar-limit matrix N for which \Gamma^{[-1]}\circ N has a negative principal minor is the direct finite-dimensional falsifier of the same-theory OS bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Supplies the finite-dimensional algebraic reason why K is the correct invariant and why pair-dependent Wilson boundary factors are not harmless normalizations.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Nonzero logarithmic cross-ratio gives a finite Schur-multiplier obstruction. If a multiplicative boundary anomaly \Gamma has K_{ik;jl}\ne0 on a finite Wilson OS core, then the same-theory transfer N\ge0 \Rightarrow M=\Gamma^{[-1]}\circ N\ge0 is not universally valid unless the reciprocal anomaly is a positive Schur multiplier. Under the additional hypothesis that both \Gamma and \Gamma^{[-1]} are positive Schur multipliers on all finite submatrices of the core, \Gamma must be rank one, hence all K vanish.

control_decision.promotion_test: Promote the bridge if one proves a valid no-connected-boundary-anomaly theorem: A=0 and K_{ik;jl}=0 for every finite matrix in a dense mirror-smooth Wilson core, with OS-density extending to the full gauge-invariant algebra.

dependency_updates.description: The Wilson test algebra should be stratified by reflection-plane boundary footprints. Separated-footprint Wilson observables form a tractable subcore; coincident-footprint/hairpin observables are the decisive obstruction class.

The topology must control finite reflected Wilson product matrices and their collar trace limits, not just individual gauge-invariant distributions. It must be strong enough to define K_{ik;jl} as a valid continuum invariant.

falsifiers: Separated-footprint falsifier: find four Wilson collar families whose boundary footprints remain a positive distance apart in the reflection plane but whose logarithmic anomaly cross-ratio K_{ik;jl} is nonzero after cutoff removal.

Coincident-footprint falsifier: compute the reflected Wilson boundary OPE for a hairpin/cusp family and find a finite connected post-subtraction term whose four-point finite difference K does not vanish.

Additive-contact falsifier: diagonal trace continuity holds but an off-diagonal additive contact remains; this would show the contact is not a positive OS contribution or that the same-theory diagonal locking was false.

Topology falsifier: the RG cutoff-removal topology gives convergence of individual Wilson loops but not of the reflected products S(\Theta W(T_\delta C_i)W(T_\delta D_j)), so the fixed-collar matrix N is not a valid limit.

Observable-algebra falsifier: eliminating K requires adding pair-dependent boundary counterterms or changing Wilson-loop renormalization at t=0; then positivity may hold, but not for the intended same theory.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 187 isolates a sharper invariant-preservation mechanism. One-body Wilson boundary renormalizations are harmless because they are diagonal congruences; additive positive contacts vanish once diagonal trace continuity is valid; and separated boundary footprints should have no connected anomaly by locality. Therefore the entire same-theory OS obstruction is the connected coincident-footprint Wilson boundary OPE, measured by the logarithmic cross-ratio K. A nonzero K is a genuine falsifier, while K=0 on a dense Wilson core would promote the reflection-positivity closed-cone bridge from formal topology to a real Yang-Mills continuum passage lemma.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the leading-order reflected Wilson collar cross-ratio for four mirror-smooth hairpin loops with the same boundary point but varied tangent/curvature, after subtracting perimeter and cusp one-body terms. In parallel, prove the easier separated-footprint estimate B=0 using locality of the regulated covariance/RG kernel to certify the first nontrivial valid subcore.
